dse_runs.notes: System spec: bursts of 8 requests, Poisson 2 req/us, p99 latency <= 0.4us. Latency is dominated by per-request service time, so favour low n_iter / pipelined families with high throughput; sys_* numbers are optimistic bounds until L2 simulation. Minimise luts_plus_ffs subject to throughput_msps>=2 and max_abs_err<=2^-10.

final_text: The single spec in the queue, **bursty_offload**, is finalized. L1: `run_dse` spent the full 400-eval budget (4 rounds, architect path refine→map_front→map_front→stop) and returned a 43-design feasible, non-dominated front over min luts_plus_ffs / max accuracy_bits, with the top-6 all `pipelined_m` designs. L2: `simulate_system` on the top 5 showed the analytic p99 bounds were optimistic by ~1.3–1.4× (winner 0.146 → 0.195 µs simulated), but every shortlisted design still passed the 0.4 µs p99 constraint and the L1 winner was unchanged. L3–L5 (via the `ladder` subagent): `verify_rtl` and `synthesize` had no recorded rows for this design and `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data`, so no WINNER CHANGE was flagged and `reexplore` was correctly skipped. The spec was finalized by its rule (min luts_plus_ffs) on `pipelined_m:data_width=16,n_iter=12,angle_guard=-1,frac_guard=1,rounding=trunc,m=6` — luts_plus_ffs=786 (643 LUTs + 143 FFs), accuracy_bits=10.1, max_abs_err=0.000901 (2^-10.12), throughput_msps=68.5, sys_p99_latency_us=0.195 (simulated) — satisfying all three constraints (throughput ≥ 2 Msps, err ≤ 2^-10, p99 ≤ 0.4 µs). Note: memory was switched off, so the lesson note was not stored.
